extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, solicitors, and litigators drafting pleadings, injunctions, assignments, licences and other precedents under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883 (United Kingdom)
extracted.subtask_description: Templates and precedent clauses for pleadings (statements of claim and defence), injunctions, motions, and contracts (agreements, assignments, licences, mortgages) relating to patents, designs and trade marks under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Claim — Infringement of Copyright in a Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Form elements for a plaintiff's statement of claim in an action for infringement of copyright in a registered design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As framed: (1) Allegation that the defendant has infringed the plaintiff's copyright in a registered design, specifying the registered design number, class and date of registration; (2) A description of the registered design ("The said registered design is [describe the design]"); (3) Allegation that the plaintiff duly caused the prescribed mark to be duly marked on all articles to which the design was applied, before delivery on sale; (4) Set out the acts complained of with reference to s.59. Relief claimed: injunction (state particular injunction sought) and a sum for damages. (Use the model on action for infringing Trade Mark, R.S.C. 1883, App. C.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Defence — Infringement of Copyright in a Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical defence pleas in a design copyright infringement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible defences to plead include: (1) The defendant did not infringe; (2) The alleged design was not duly registered; (3) The copyright had expired prior to the alleged acts complained of; (4) The plaintiff did not cause each article to be marked with the prescribed mark before delivery on sale, nor take proper steps to ensure marking, and the copyright had expired prior to the acts complained of. Add any other factual denials or particulars as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction restraining infringement of Copyright in a Design (form and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and operative terms for an injunction restraining infringement of copyright in a design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usual undertaking required. Example operative language: restrain the defendant, his servants and agents from selling the design in the statement of claim and from applying the same or any colourable imitation thereof to any substance or article of manufacture; in particular prohibit manufacturing and selling articles (example: ornamental sweetmeats) made so as to resemble the plaintiff's. Specify prohibited acts (manufacture, apply, sell, offer for sale, expose for sale) and identify particular articles by reference to the statement of claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order continuing injunction; delivery up of articles; payment of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Form order continuing and enforcing an injunction with mandatory relief and costs directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical terms: continue the injunction until a specified date; order defendants to deliver up for destruction drawings, point paper, cards used in applying the design and articles manufactured by defendant to which the design was applied (verification by affidavit); refer to the taxing master to tax reasonable and proper costs as between party and party and certify amount; defendants to pay taxed costs and, on payment, further proceedings to be stayed unless injunction breached. Include liberty to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Claim — Infringing a Trade Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Form elements for plaintiff's claim in a trade mark infringement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allege (1) the defendant has infringed the plaintiff's trade mark; (2) describe the trade mark; (3) if plaintiff is not original proprietor, show briefly how title is derived; (4) set out the acts complained of. Relief claimed: injunction (state particular injunction sought) and an account or damages. Use R.S.C. 1883 App. C s.6 No.8 as model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Defence — Trade Mark Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical defensive pleas in a trade mark infringement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defences to plead may include: (1) The trade mark is not the plaintiff's (i.e., no title); (2) The alleged trade mark is not a trade mark (invalid as a mark); (3) The defendant did not infringe. Add appropriate factual particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Motion to restrain use of a Registered Trade Mark (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and operative prayer for a Notice of Motion to restrain use of a registered trade mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include formal parts as in Notice of Motion to restrain infringement of a Patent. Pray for an order restraining defendant until further order from infringing the plaintiff's trade mark registered under the Act and from selling or offering for sale any goods (example: tea) or using wrappers imprinted with imitation or colourable imitation of the plaintiff's mark. Tailor goods/acts in prayer to particulars of claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Order restraining use of a Registered Trade Mark (form and undertaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of interlocutory order granting interim relief against use of a registered trade mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usual undertaking as to damages required. Order to restrain defendant until a specified date or further order from infringing the plaintiff's registered trade marks and from selling or offering for sale goods or using wrappers with any imitation or colourable imitation of the plaintiff's marks. Include liberty to apply and typical interlocutory costs consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual injunction with account of profits and costs (example: 'Eureka')
rubrics_metrics.description: Form terms for a final/perpetual injunction in trade mark cases including ancillary monetary relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language: perpetually restrain defendants and agents from applying the mark/title to any shirts manufactured by defendants or sold by them unless manufactured by the plaintiff and with his sanction; restrain issuing boxes/packages bearing the mark on shirts not of the plaintiff; order an account of profits made by defendants in manufacturing and selling under the mark since a particular date; direct defendants to pay amount certified within specified days; order repayment of taxed costs paid by plaintiff to defendants within specified days; defendants to pay plaintiff's costs of action (including interlocutory costs), except costs occasioned by appeal. Include liberty to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction restraining use of Trade Mark on specified goods (cutlery example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific prohibitions that an injunction may impose in relation to marks on particular goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example terms: restrain defendants from stamping, cutting or engraving, or causing to be stamped, cut or engraved upon any tools or other articles manufactured for, bought, procured or sold by them, specified words or words similar or colourably differing, or any words/marks contrived so as to represent or lead to belief that articles were of the plaintiff's manufacture; restrain affixing/using labels similar or colourably differing from the plaintiff's labels; restrain selling/exporting/disposing of articles bearing such offending marks or labels. Draft prohibitions to cover methods of marking/branding specific to the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affixing tickets or using plaintiff's design on tickets (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model injunction where the dispute concerns tickets/labels and use of distinguishing features or devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example terms: restrain defendants, their servants and agents from fixing or causing to be affixed to goods (example: Turkey-red yarn not dyed by plaintiffs) a particular ticket (marked B.) and from using specified devices (e.g., two elephants) on tickets without clearly distinguishing such ticket from the plaintiff's ticket (exhibit A) or so as to represent or induce belief that yarn was dyed by plaintiffs. Ancillary relief: order for an account of profits and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction restraining use of a Brand as a Trade Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Form injunction to prevent affixing a brand/mark to goods so as to represent origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language: restrain defendants from affixing to casks of wine the brand/marks of a crown and the word 'Seixo', or any other combination so contrived by colourable imitation to represent plaintiff's marks; restrain employing marks/words so as to represent or induce belief that wines are of plaintiff's produce; require defendants to distinguish use from plaintiff's goods. Draft to prevent false representation/inducement of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement for sale of Patent subject to payment of royalties — required clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential clauses to include when selling a patent subject to royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model provisions include: (1) sale/purchase recitals identifying the patent (title, date, number) and purchase price payable by a specified date; (2) royalty covenant: buyer shall pay seller a specified sum for every article manufactured according to the patent and sold by buyer, with timing (e.g., half-yearly settlements) and first payment date; (3) accounts: annual or half-yearly settlement dates; (4) obligation on buyer to take proceedings for infringement at his own cost, with seller entitled to determine agreement if buyer defaults; (5) clause making agreement void if letters patent or any extension be judicially determined invalid (without prejudice to recovery of monies due); (6) provision allowing seller to determine agreement if buyer discontinues manufacture or fails to sell a minimum quantity in a year; (7) successor provisions on buyer's death (time to enter into substituted agreement) with consequences if not complied with. Include standard execution clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Form of Assignment of Letters Patent — core assignment language
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise indenture form effecting assignment of letters patent and exclusive benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical wording assigns and transfers to the assignee (and their executors, administrators and assigns) all that the inventor's invention and the letters patent and the full and exclusive benefit thereof, and of any improvement, extension or renewal and the right to apply for and obtain extension/renewal, and all rights, powers and benefits thereto for the residue of the term of fourteen years and any further period by extension/prolongation. Note footnote: words 'beneficial owner' will imply covenants for title but not covenant as to validity of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Form of Licence — grant language (concise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief licence form granting right to use and vend an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model grant: in consideration of a sum, the licensor grants to the licensee (and his executors, administrators and assigns) [the sole, full and exclusive] licence to use and exercise the invention during a specified term and to sell and dispose of all manufactured according to the invention for the licensee's absolute use and benefit. Optional bracketed words allow omission if licence not to be transmissible/assignable or not to be exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence to use Patent (long form) — covenants, payments and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive licence form clauses and usual contractual protections for licensor and licensor rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: recitals identifying patent; grant clause (sole/full/exclusive or limited to geographic area); royalty covenant specifying amount per unit, payment periods (e.g., every half year), and due dates; obligation on licensee to furnish full written account within specified days after each accounting period, with entries/statement verifiable by statutory declaration if required; licensor's inspection right to enter place of business at reasonable hours to inspect works and stock; licencee's right/duty to take proceedings for infringement at his own cost but in the name of the licensor; prohibition on assignment/sub-licensing without consent (omit transmissible words if restriction intended); proviso allowing determination on notice after stated period; revocation on arrears, bankruptcy, insolvency, or breach of covenants (right to revoke by notice); licence void on licensee's death (subject to monies due); clause that licensor not required to pay stamp duties to keep patent up (and licence void if patent lapses by non-payment of duties) ; express statement that licence does not create partnership; express non-warranty by licensor as to novelty, utility, validity or sufficiency of the specification or filing. Include remedies preservation language ('without prejudice to the remedies of either party').

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and remedy clauses in licences and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard grounds and procedures for determining or revoking licences/agreements and preserving remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical grounds: non-payment of royalties (arrears after specified period), bankruptcy or composition with creditors, default in covenant performance, death of licensee (where applicable), or judicial determination of patent invalidity (renders agreement void). Remedies/procedures: right to revoke by notice in writing, provision that revocation/determination is 'without prejudice' to recovery of monies then due or other remedies, and requirement to give specified calendar months' notice for determination in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting, verification and inspection clauses (in licences/assignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model provisions governing royalty accounting, verification and licensor's inspection rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require licensee/buyer to keep books, furnish within specified days after each accounting period a full account and statement in writing of all articles manufactured or sold, require statements and entries to be verified by statutory declaration if required, and permit the licensor at any time during licence to enter the licensee's place of business at any reasonable hour to inspect works and goods and any in course of manufacture. Provide for taxation/verification of delivered up articles by affidavit where delivery up is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to prosecute infringements (contractual allocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who must commence and bear cost of infringement proceedings under sale/licence agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical provision: the buyer/licensee shall at his own cost take all necessary proceedings for effectually protecting and defending the patent/letters patent (i.e., sue for infringement) and, in default of so doing, the seller/licensor may determine the agreement. Some forms allow the licensee to sue in the name of the patentee at licensee's cost. Include clear allocation of costs and rights to be enforced in the contractual wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamp duty and patent renewal obligations (contract clauses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who bears duty to pay stamp duties and keep patent in force; consequences of non-payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common clause: nothing in the licence shall render it incumbent on the licensor to pay stamp duties payable to keep up the patent; if patent becomes void by non-payment of such duties then the licence shall likewise become void, but without prejudice to recovery of monies then due or to remedies for antecedent breaches. For foreign patents the assignee/licensee may be required to take out patents and pay necessary and proper stamp duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of right to take out patent in foreign countries — covenants and royalty schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of assignment granting right to take out foreign patents together with detailed royalty covenant and auxiliary obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical structure: recitals identifying original grants and agent relationships; assignment of letters patent and right to take out patents in India, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and other colonies to the assignee; separate covenants by assignors as to validity of patents (covenant that letters patent are good, valid and effectual); covenant by assignee to pay specified royalties (often detailed schedules, e.g., sums per engine constructed depending on shaft depth, additional sums for safety apparatus, etc.); reductions for first four orders (discounted royalty for initial orders); division/allocation of royalties between parties (e.g., specific fractions to parties for first orders and subsequent orders); covenant for assignee to use best endeavours to take out foreign patents, pay necessary duties and further the introduction and sale of protected goods within specified limits; obligation to keep accounts, books and particulars of licences granted and consideration reserved, and supply names/particulars as required.
